name: Add project_id to message
description:
1. **Problem 1 — diffs:** `CodeViewer` always used the chat's project for diff/read requests, so blocks from a message with its own `project_id` loaded an empty/incorrect diff; `effectiveProject` was reordered to `messageProject → project prop → chatProject`.
2. **Problem 2 — writes:** `save-file` carried only `{ file, content }`, so `Chat.vue#onSaveFile` wrote through `$storex.chats.writeFile` using the chat's `codx_path` and the write failed (silently) whenever the block belonged to another project.
3. **Fix spread:** `CodeViewer` now emits `project: this.effectiveProject` with `save-file` and routes `runScript`/`run.patch` through `this.$api`; `Chat.vue#onSaveFile` writes via that project's `$api.files.write` (store fallback) and surfaces failures.
4. **Bulk save:** `ChatEntry` gained `codeWriteProject` (`messageProject → chatProject → $project`) for `files.writeMultiple` and tags its fallback `save-file` emissions with it.
5. **Impact:** all code-block API calls (write, bulk write, diff, read, rollback, patch, run-script) now use the message's project when present, with behaviour unchanged when no `project_id` is set; `store/project.js#codeImprovePatch`/`generateCode` flagged as a follow-up.

messages.content: Add project_id to message. Now messages can define a project_id. Use ProjectDetailt

I'll start by understanding the current state of the codebase around messages and projects.## 1. Review & Understand the Task - **Goal:** messages can now target a project, i.e. carry a `project_id`. - **Change surface:** - `Message` model gains `project_id`. - The shared `getUserMessage()` factory includes `project_id` when building a message. - The composer gets a project picker so the user chooses which project a message is addressed to — reusing the existing `ProjectDetailt` component. - **Constraints:** keep the Vue options-API structure of the touched files, keep changes minimal and reviewable, reuse existing components (`ProjectDetailt`, `ChatLLMModelSelector`, `ChatProfileSelector` pattern), DaisyUI + Tailwind only. ## 2. Information Gathering (from the codebase) - `src/components/ProjectDetailt.vue` → props `modelValue` (project object, falls back to `$project`), `iconify`; emits `update:modelValue`, `select`, `open`, `close`. - Composer chain: `Chat.vue` → `ChatInputBox.vue` → `ChatInputToolbar.vue`; each hop forwards props/emits (existing pattern: `selectedModel` / `model-changed`, `selectedProfiles` / `profiles-selected`). - Message creation: `src/service/chat.js#getUserMessage()`; editing: `Chat.vue#updateMessage()` → `chatSvc.updateExistingMessage()`. - Project registry: `$projects.allProjectsById[project_id]`; the chat's working project is `Chat.vue#chatProject`. ## 3. Changes Summary | File | Change | |---|---| | `src/components/chat/ChatInputToolbar.vue` | Renders a `ProjectDetailt` picker (project the message is addressed to), a "back to chat project" reset button, emits `project-changed`. | | `src/components/chat/ChatInputBox.vue` | Forwards `project` / `chatProject` props and the `project-changed` emit to the toolbar. | | `src/components/chat/Chat.vue` | Holds `messageProject`, passes it to the composer, sends `project_id` on new/edited messages, restores it in edit mode and clears it after sending. | | `src/service/chat.js` | `getUserMessage()` accepts and stores `project_id`. | | `src/model/chat.ts` | `Message.project_id?: string`. | ## 4. The Changes getUserMessage({ message, files, profiles, attachments, metadata, user, taskItem, task_item, project_id }) { return { role: "user", content: message, // Project this message is addressed to. When omitted the chat's project applies. project_id, files, profiles, attachments, task_item: taskItem, user: user || this.$user.username, meta_data: metadata, done: true, task_item, } } export interface Message { doc_id?: string role: string task_item: string content: string think?: string hide: boolean is_answer: boolean improvement: boolean created_at: string updated_at: string images: string[] files: string[] meta_data?: Record profiles: string[] user?: string knowledge_topics: string[] done?: boolean is_thinking?: boolean disable_knowledge?: boolean read_by: string[] error?: string cost?: number cost_info?: Record // Project this message is addressed to. Overrides the chat's project when set. project_id?: string } selectedUser: null, // Project the next message is addressed to (message.project_id). // `null` keeps the chat's project, which is the default behaviour. messageProject: null, showDocumentSearchModal: false, :profiles="profiles" :selected-profiles="selectedProfiles" :project="messageTargetProject" :chat-project="chatProject" :cursor-word="cursorWord" :voice-language-label="$ui.voiceLanguages?.[$ui.voiceLanguage]" :chat="chat" :collapsed="inputCollapsed" :attachment-count="attachments?.length || 0" :file-count="files?.length || 0" @send="sendMessage" @add-message="addNewMessage()" @search-message="addSearchMessage" @cancel-edit="onResetEdit" @paste="onContentPaste" @keydown="onChatInputKeyDown" @drop.stop="onDropInputBox" @model-changed="onLLMModelChanged" @profiles-selected="onProfilesSelected" @project-changed="onMessageProjectChanged" @upload-files="onUploadFiles" @toggle-voice="toggleVoiceSession" @toggle-collapsed="toggleInputCollapsed" /> chatProject() { return this.$projects.allProjectsById[this.chat.project_id || this.chat.owner_project_id] || this.$project }, // Project the message being composed is addressed to: the explicitly selected // one or, by default, the chat's working project. messageTargetProject() { return this.messageProject || this.chatProject }, onProfilesSelected(selectedProfiles) { this.selectorProfileNames = selectedProfiles.map(p => p.name || p) }, // Selecting the chat's own project (or clearing it) falls back to the default // instead of storing a redundant copy on the message. onMessageProjectChanged(project) { const projectId = project?.project_id this.messageProject = !projectId || projectId === this.chatProject?.project_id ? null : project }, getUserMessage({ message, task_item }) { return this.chatSvc.getUserMessage({ message, project_id: this.messageProject?.project_id, files: this.chatSvc.getMessageFiles({ messageMentions: this.messageMentions, files: this.files }), profiles: [...new Set([...this.selectorProfileNames, ...this.textProfileNames])], attachments: this.attachments.map(a => a.toJSON?.() || a), metadata: this.metadata, user: this.$user.username, task_item }) }, const files = this.messageMentions.filter(m => m.file).map(m => m.file) const update = { content, profiles, files, attachments: this.attachments.map(a => a.toJSON?.() || a), updated_at: new Date().toISOString() } // Only send the project when the composer targets a different one, so // editing a message never drops its stored project_id. if (this.messageProject?.project_id) update.project_id = this.messageProject.project_id try { await this.chatSvc.updateExistingMessage({ chat: this.chat, doc_id: message.doc_id, update }) this.editMessage = message this.setEditorText(message.content || '') this.selectorProfileNames = [...(message.profiles || [])] this.messageProject = message.project_id ? this.$projects.allProjectsById[message.project_id] || null : null this.files = [...(message.files || [])] onResetEdit() { this.editMessage = null this.editMessageId = null this.setEditorText('') this.files = [] this.attachments = [] this.messageProject = null this.selectorProfileNames = [] cleanUserInputAndWaitAnswer() { this.setEditorText("") this.attachments = [] this.files = [] this.mentions = [] this.messageProject = null this.textProfileNames = [] ## 5. Notes / Behavior - **Default stays unchanged:** the picker shows the chat's project; unless another project is chosen, `project_id` is `undefined` and the backend keeps using the chat's project. No migration needed for existing messages. - **Override is visible:** when the message targets another project, the project button (via `ProjectDetailt`) shows it and a small amber reset button appears (`w-…` compact; icon-only on mobile). - **Edit flow:** editing restores the message's `project_id` into the picker and only re-sends `project_id` when an override is present. - **Accessibility:** reset action has `aria-label` + `data-tip`; `ProjectDetailt`'s icon carries `alt` with the project name, and the reset button keeps a visible focus ring via DaisyUI `btn`. Optional follow-up (not included, to keep this reviewable): render the message's `project_id` as a badge in `ChatEntry` headers so the target project of past messages is visible in the conversation.
